subject: Reversible jump mcmc with an interaction term

messages.author: e10074edba72b727
messages.subject: Reversible jump mcmc with an interaction term
parts:
Hello,

I am using nimble to run the Spatial Count model (Royle, Chandler SCR Book, spatial model to estimate species abundance/density from camera counts).  I am evaluating the detection portion with a linear predictor with 2 covariates and an interaction term:


Log(lamda0) = beta0 + beta[1]* snow + beta[2]*temperature + beta[3] * snow * temperature


I am using reversible jump mcmc to do model selection and my question is a about how to implement this with the interaction term. I am using indicator variable and have experimented using reversible jump a couple of ways:


1. single indicator for the interaction..

Log(lamda0) = beta0 + indicator[1]* beta[1]* snow + indicator[2]* beta[2]*temperature

+ indicator[3]* beta[3] * snow * temperature


2. combined indicators for the interaction..

Log(lamda0) = beta0 + indicator[1]* beta[1]* snow + indicator[2]* beta[2]*temperature

          + indicator[1]* indicator[2]* indicator[3]* beta[3] * snow * temperature

 

Both of these models run and give surprisingly similar results in my testing, but I am not sure if either one is appropriate.  I have hunted around the web/literature a bit but have not found a clear answer.

One follow up question, in my tests (both cases above, run on coyote data from a camera trap array), I get pretty low numbers for the indicator posterior means (like .18 for the interaction, and really low for the individual covariates (around .01 to .001).  Are these numbers simply suggesting that there is not much support for the covariates in the model (in other words support for the dot model), or should the indicator means be interpreted relative to each other?  I don’t think that a reproducible example is needed here, but please let me know if anyone thinks otherwise and I could try to supply something.

Thank you. 

Brian

messages.author: ac2eba1e47ae807d
messages.subject: Re: Reversible jump mcmc with an interaction term
parts:
Hi Brian,

sorry for the late reply on this. I think that option 2 makes sense, interaction should be in the model if both main effects are. The drawback of option 2 is that the interaction coefficient would be sampled even when it is not in the model.  To prevent this, I'd suggest you to use dconstraint. In this way you can force indicator[3] to be equal to 1 only when both the main effects are in the model. In model code

constraint ~ dconstraint(indicator[1] >= indicator[3] & indicator[2] >= indicator[3])

Log(lamda0) = beta0 + indicator[1]* beta[1]* snow + indicator[2]* beta[2]*temperature
+ indicator[3]* beta[3] * snow * temperature

and you can set the value of constraint in the data, i.e. data$constraint = 1. If the condition is violated, the likelihood for dconstraint is zero, which is used whenever a change to any of indicator[1], indicator[2], indicator[3] is proposed.

Make sure to initialize the model with values that satisfy the constraint. This should help to adjust inclusion probabilities.  Note also that with this constraint, the RJMCMC would not remove a main effect unless all of its interactions are out of the model, which may result in slow mixing. Feel free to follow up on this!

Best, 

Sally
